# Two-group random-intercept repeated-measures study power calculation
# Analysis method: participant-level averages with pooled t-test

# Study parameters
m <- 4           # observations per participant
marginal_sd <- 1 # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4       # intraclass correlation (ICC)
delta <- 0.45    # group mean difference
alpha <- 0.05    # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Derived variance parameters
# Var(Y_ij) = tau^2 + sigma^2 = 1
# rho = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) = 0.4
tau_sq <- rho           # random-intercept variance
sigma_sq <- 1 - rho     # within-participant error variance

cat("=== Variance Decomposition ===\n")
cat("Marginal variance: Var(Y_ij) =", marginal_sd^2, "\n")
cat("Random-intercept variance (tau^2):", tau_sq, "\n")
cat("Within-participant error variance (sigma^2):", sigma_sq, "\n")
cat("ICC = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) =", tau_sq / (tau_sq + sigma_sq), "\n\n")

# Variance of participant-level averages
# Var(Y_bar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m
var_participant_mean <- tau_sq + sigma_sq / m
sd_participant_mean <- sqrt(var_participant_mean)

cat("=== Participant-Level Average Distribution ===\n")
cat("Var(Y_bar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m =", tau_sq, "+", sigma_sq/m, "=", var_participant_mean, "\n")
cat("SD(Y_bar_i) =", sd_participant_mean, "\n\n")

# Pooled standard error for comparing two groups
# SE = sd_participant_mean * sqrt(2/n) = sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2/n)
# t-statistic: t = delta / SE = delta / sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2/n)
# Non-centrality: lambda = delta / SE for fixed n

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
calc_power <- function(n, delta, var_pm, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  # Standard error: SE = sqrt(var_pm * 2/n)
  se <- sqrt(var_pm * 2 / n)
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- delta / se
  # Critical value (two-sided)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  # Power: P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp) + pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(1, 100)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calc_power(n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_search[powers >= target_power])

cat("=== Power Calculation Results ===\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Group mean difference:", delta, "\n")
cat("Participant-level SD:", sd_participant_mean, "\n\n")

# Display powers around the minimum
display_range <- max(1, min_n - 2) : (min_n + 2)
for (n in display_range) {
  pw <- calc_power(n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha)
  se <- sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2 / n)

}

cat("\n=== ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group (integer):", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", calc_power(min_n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", calc_power(min_n - 1, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output

  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

# Include additional verification metrics

  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = achieved_power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "preceding_sample_size", value = min_n - 1, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_n", value = preceding_power, unit = "probability")
  )
)

cat("=== DETAILED MODEL VERIFICATION ===\n\n")

# Parameters
m <- 4
rho <- 0.4
sigma2_marginal <- 1  # marginal variance = 1

# From ICC definition: rho = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) where tau^2 + sigma^2 = sigma2_marginal
tau_sq <- rho * sigma2_marginal
sigma_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma2_marginal

cat("1. VARIANCE DECOMPOSITION\n")
cat("   Random-intercept model: Y_ij = mu_i + epsilon_ij\n")
cat("   where mu_i ~ N(0, tau^2) and epsilon_ij ~ N(0, sigma^2)\n")
cat("   ICC = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) =", rho, "\n")
cat("   Given marginal variance = 1, we solve:\n")
cat("   tau^2 + sigma^2 = 1 and tau^2/(tau^2+sigma^2) = 0.4\n")
cat("   => tau^2 =", tau_sq, "and sigma^2 =", sigma_sq, "\n\n")

# Variance of individual observation
var_individual <- tau_sq + sigma_sq
cat("2. INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL VARIANCE\n")
cat("   Var(Y_ij) = tau^2 + sigma^2 =", var_individual, "\n\n")

# Variance of participant average
var_avg <- tau_sq + sigma_sq / m
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("3. PARTICIPANT-AVERAGE VARIANCE\n")
cat("   When computing Ybar_i = (1/m) * sum_j Y_ij:\n")
cat("   Var(Ybar_i) = Var(mu_i + (1/m)*sum_j epsilon_ij)\n")
cat("              = Var(mu_i) + Var((1/m)*sum_j epsilon_ij)\n")
cat("              = tau^2 + (1/m^2) * m * sigma^2   [independent random effects]\n")
cat("              = tau^2 + sigma^2/m\n")
cat("              =", tau_sq, "+", sigma_sq/m, "\n")
cat("              =", var_avg, "\n")
cat("   SD(Ybar_i) =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective correlation structure comment
cat("4. CORRELATION STRUCTURE\n")
cat("   Within-participant correlation (exchangeable):\n")
cat("   Cov(Y_ij, Y_ij') = tau^2 for j ≠ j'\n")
cat("   Correlation = tau^2 / Var(Y_ij) = tau^2 / 1 =", tau_sq, "\n")
cat("   This matches the specified ICC = 0.4 ✓\n\n")

# Two-sample t-test specification
cat("5. TWO-SAMPLE T-TEST SPECIFICATION\n")
cat("   H0: E(Ybar_1) = E(Ybar_2), vs H1: E(Ybar_1) - E(Ybar_2) = 0.45\n")
cat("   Assumption: Ybar_i ~ N(mu_group, Var(Ybar_i)) independently\n")
cat("   Test statistic: t = (Ybar_1 - Ybar_2) / sqrt(s_p^2 * (2/n))\n")
cat("   where s_p^2 is the pooled sample variance, approximately = Var(Ybar_i)\n")
cat("   Under H0: t ~ t_{2n-2}\n")
cat("   Under H1: t ~ t_{2n-2}(lambda) with lambda = 0.45 / sqrt(Var(Ybar_i)*2/n)\n\n")

Significance level α = 0.05

scientific_notes: The marginal variance decomposition in a random-intercept model: Var(Y_{ij}) = τ² + σ² = 1, where τ² is the random-intercept variance and σ² is the within-participant error variance. The intraclass correlation is ρ = τ²/(τ²+σ²) = 0.4, implying τ² = 0.4 and σ² = 0.6.

The effective standard deviation of participant means is √0.55 ≈ 0.7416, pooled across groups.
The t-test compares two group means with pooled standard error SE = √0.55 × √(2/n), where n is the per-group sample size.
Non-centrality parameter for the t-test: Δ/SE = 0.45 / √(1.1/n) = 0.45√(n/1.1).

# Two-group random-intercept repeated-measures study power calculation
# Analysis method: participant-level averages with pooled t-test

# Study parameters
m <- 4           # observations per participant
marginal_sd <- 1 # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4       # intraclass correlation (ICC)
delta <- 0.45    # group mean difference
alpha <- 0.05    # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Derived variance parameters
# Var(Y_ij) = tau^2 + sigma^2 = 1
# rho = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) = 0.4
tau_sq <- rho           # random-intercept variance
sigma_sq <- 1 - rho     # within-participant error variance

cat("=== Variance Decomposition ===\n")
cat("Marginal variance: Var(Y_ij) =", marginal_sd^2, "\n")
cat("Random-intercept variance (tau^2):", tau_sq, "\n")
cat("Within-participant error variance (sigma^2):", sigma_sq, "\n")
cat("ICC = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) =", tau_sq / (tau_sq + sigma_sq), "\n\n")

# Variance of participant-level averages
# Var(Y_bar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m
var_participant_mean <- tau_sq + sigma_sq / m
sd_participant_mean <- sqrt(var_participant_mean)

cat("=== Participant-Level Average Distribution ===\n")
cat("Var(Y_bar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m =", tau_sq, "+", sigma_sq/m, "=", var_participant_mean, "\n")
cat("SD(Y_bar_i) =", sd_participant_mean, "\n\n")

# Pooled standard error for comparing two groups
# SE = sd_participant_mean * sqrt(2/n) = sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2/n)
# t-statistic: t = delta / SE = delta / sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2/n)
# Non-centrality: lambda = delta / SE for fixed n

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
calc_power <- function(n, delta, var_pm, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  # Standard error: SE = sqrt(var_pm * 2/n)
  se <- sqrt(var_pm * 2 / n)
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- delta / se
  # Critical value (two-sided)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  # Power: P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp) + pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(1, 100)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calc_power(n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_search[powers >= target_power])

cat("=== Power Calculation Results ===\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Group mean difference:", delta, "\n")
cat("Participant-level SD:", sd_participant_mean, "\n\n")

# Display powers around the minimum
display_range <- max(1, min_n - 2) : (min_n + 2)
for (n in display_range) {
  pw <- calc_power(n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha)
  se <- sqrt(var_participant_mean * 2 / n)
  ncp <- delta / se
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  cat(sprintf("n = %3d (df = %4d): SE = %.6f, ncp = %.6f, power = %.6f\n", 
              n, df, se, ncp, pw))
}

cat("\n=== ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group (integer):", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", calc_power(min_n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", calc_power(min_n - 1, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

# Include additional verification metrics
achieved_power <- calc_power(min_n, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha)
preceding_power <- calc_power(min_n - 1, delta, var_participant_mean, alpha)

cat("\n=== JSON Result ===\n")

  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = achieved_power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "preceding_sample_size", value = min_n - 1, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_n", value = preceding_power, unit = "probability")

)

# From ICC definition: rho = tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2) = marginal_sd^2

cat("  Verification: tau^2 + sigma^2 =", tau_sq + sigma_sq, "\n\n")

# Participant-level average variance
# When we average m=4 observations per participant:
# Var(Ybar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m
var_ybar <- tau_sq + sigma_sq/m
sd_ybar <- sqrt(var_ybar)

cat("Participant average distribution:\n")
cat("  Var(Ybar_i) = tau^2 + sigma^2/m\n")
cat("            = ", tau_sq, "+", sigma_sq, "/", m, "\n")
cat("            = ", tau_sq, "+", sigma_sq/m, "\n")
cat("            = ", var_ybar, "\n")
cat("  SD(Ybar_i) = ", sd_ybar, "\n\n")

# Two-sample t-test on participant means
# Under H0: both groups have same mean
# Under H1: group difference = delta = 0.45
# Each group has n participants
# Test statistic: t = (Ybar_1 - Ybar_2) / SE, where SE = SD(Ybar_i) * sqrt(2/n)
# df = 2n - 2

# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = delta / SE = delta / sqrt(var_ybar * 2/n)
#                                  = delta * sqrt(n / (2*var_ybar))

power_calc <- function(n) {
  df <- 2*n - 2
  se <- sqrt(var_ybar * 2/n)
  lambda <- delta / se
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  
  # Power = P(|t| > t_crit | H1 with ncp = lambda)
  # This is P(t > t_crit) + P(t < -t_crit) under non-central t with ncp = lambda
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
